pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Highly irregular, dendritic-edged dark regions with high-contrast sharp pixel gradients; geometry resembles fractal or oak-leaf patterns rather than smooth polygons.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Interconnected light-tan pathways forming a non-uniform topological graph; pathways show variable thickness and frequent irregular junction nodes.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Short, stiff hair line along the dorsal neck boundary exhibiting a low-amplitude, high-frequency jagged silhouette against the background.
dorsal_ridge_profile.contour_gaps: Visible structural break in mane continuity near the lower-neck junction where the silhouette flattens.

focal_dorsal_anomalies.chronic_feeding_lesions: Localized dark, raised textural masses on the mid-lateral neck surface, currently serving as attachment points for avian organisms.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Presence of two dark-toned avian ectoparasite cleaners (oxpeckers) physically attached to the mane and lateral neck skin.
other_distinctive_markers: Partial occlusion of the primary subject by a second foreground specimen in the lower-left quadrant, which exhibits contrasting high-luminance, smooth-edged rectangular pelage patches.
